key_insight: Engineered surfaces require hierarchical, multi-modal NDE that pairs rapid screening with calibrated confirmation tailored to surface and interface physics.
engineering_relevance: Targeted inspection can support quality and service-life assessment of coatings, cold-sprayed deposits, laser-clad overlays, and additively manufactured surface regions.
method: Match inspection physics to thickness, adhesion, stress, porosity, and interface defects.
Review electromagnetic, thermal, acoustic, optical, and X-ray inspection capabilities and limitations.
Assess in-process sensing, data fusion, physics-informed machine learning, and digital twins.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a review of method capabilities and limitations, not a new experimental benchmark or quantitative validation.
watch_item: Deployment remains constrained by limited probability-of-detection evidence, scarce reference specimens, weak model transferability, and incomplete acceptance criteria.
paper_title: Non-Destructive Evaluation for Engineered Surfaces: Methods, In-Process Sensing, and Data-Driven Inspection in the NDE 4.0 Era
